title: NIST, UMD, and Qunnect Demonstrate Quantum Entanglement Over 62 km Metropolitan Aerial Fiber - Quantum Computing Report
gist: NIST, the Joint Quantum Institute at the University of Maryland, and startup Qunnect distributed polarization-entangled photons over 62 km of live, partially aerial commercial telecom fiber between Gaithersburg and College Park, holding a CHSH parameter of S=2.45±0.08 with 92.8% link uptime across a 24-hour run. The result's commercial significance is that metropolitan quantum networks, QKD channels and distributed quantum computing interconnects can ride existing unshielded pole-mounted fiber, removing the need for custom buried installations — with Qunnect's automated polarization compensation as the enabling component.

insights.claim: Aerial fiber suspended from utility poles suffers severe polarization drift from wind, traffic vibration and daily ambient temperature swings, whereas buried subterranean fiber stays thermally and mechanically isolated — making pole-mounted routes the hard case for entanglement distribution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Aerial spans dominate existing metro and last-mile plant, so solving drift there is what unlocks quantum networking on already-deployed infrastructure rather than new-build routes.
insights.quote: aerial fiber suspended from utility poles experiences severe polarization drift due to wind, traffic vibrations, and ambient daily temperature swings
insights.locator: Unlike buried subterranean fiber optic lines

insights.claim: Qunnect's automated polarization compensation multiplexes reference light beams through the same fiber to continuously map time-varying birefringence, then calculates and applies inverse unitary transformations in real time to preserve the photons' quantum polarization state.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is the reusable mechanism turning noisy commercial fiber into a quantum channel; it is a compensation-electronics problem, not a new-fiber problem, which points value at component vendors rather than carriers.
insights.quote: multiplexes reference light beams through the fiber to continuously map time-varying birefringence, calculating and applying inverse unitary transformations in real-time

insights.claim: The link architecture splits functions across endpoints — an entangled photon pair source plus local signal-photon analyzer at NIST Gaithersburg, and real-time active polarization correction plus an idler receiver and time-tagging unit at UMD College Park — with a parallel optical link carried for timing synchronization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A working bill of materials for a metro quantum link: pair source, APC unit, time-tagging receiver and a synchronization channel — the shopping list to watch for supplier exposure.

insights.claim: Entangled photons were transmitted over 62 kilometers (38.5 miles) of commercial telecommunications fiber connecting NIST's Gaithersburg campus to the University of Maryland in College Park — a live, partially aerial link rather than a lab spool.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: 62 km on in-service commercial fiber sets the current practical benchmark for metro quantum links; treat it as the distance bar competing demos must clear.
insights.locator: the team transmitted entangled photons over 62 kilometers

insights.claim: A continuous 24-hour stress test sustained an entangled photon distribution rate of roughly 1,500 pairs per second across the 62 km aerial-and-buried commercial link.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pair rate is the throughput ceiling for any QKD key-generation or distributed-compute application built on such a link — 1,500 pairs/sec frames what services are economically viable today.
insights.quote: an entangled photon distribution rate of approximately 1,500 pairs per second

insights.claim: The demonstration recorded 92.8% operational link uptime, with 7.2% of total link time consumed by active polarization re-calibration — quantifying the duty-cycle tax that environmental noise imposes on aerial quantum channels.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: That 7.2% recalibration overhead is the key KPI to track: driving it down is the direct path to carrier-grade availability and is where the next round of vendor differentiation will show up.
insights.quote: an operational link uptime of 92.8% (requiring only 7.2% of total link time for active polarization re-calibration)

insights.claim: The team measured a time-averaged CHSH Bell inequality parameter of S = 2.45 ± 0.08, violating the classical threshold of S ≤ 2 for more than 20 consecutive hours on the deployed fiber.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sustained Bell violation over 20+ hours, not a momentary peak, is what separates a physics demo from an operable network asset — the standard to hold future announcements to.
insights.quote: a time-averaged Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) Bell inequality parameter of S=2.45±0.08, violating the classical physics threshold (S≤2) for over 20 consecutive hours
insights.locator: The team recorded a time-averaged Clauser

insights.claim: The trial's central claim is that metropolitan-scale quantum networks, Quantum Key Distribution channels and distributed quantum computing interconnects can be deployed over existing, unshielded commercial fiber without custom underground installations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removes trenching and civil works from the cost stack of metro quantum networking, collapsing the capex barrier and pulling forward realistic deployment timelines for QKD and multi-site quantum compute.
insights.quote: can be deployed over existing, unshielded commercial fiber infrastructure without requiring custom underground installations
insights.locator: The trial validates that metropolitan-scale quantum networks

insights.claim: With fiber civil works taken off the critical path, the binding constraint on metro quantum links shifts to active polarization compensation hardware — the piece Qunnect supplied and the layer where commercial value concentrates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Points exposure toward quantum-networking component suppliers rather than fiber owners; Qunnect is the named private beneficiary of this result.

insights.claim: The validated scope is explicitly metropolitan-scale, not long-haul: the result covers a single 62 km span with endpoint compensation and says nothing about quantum repeaters or memories needed to extend beyond metro distances.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Guards against over-extrapolation — intercity and national quantum networks remain unsolved, so discount narratives that read this as a step toward a continental quantum internet.
insights.quote: The trial validates that metropolitan-scale quantum networks
insights.locator: The trial validates that metropolitan-scale quantum networks

insights.claim: The work is peer-reviewed and open-access, published in the Journal of Optical Communications and Networking (Vol. 18, Issue 8), and was executed by a national-lab plus university plus venture-stage-startup consortium (NIST, JQI/UMD, Qunnect).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
entities: Journal of Optical Communications and Networking
insights.so_what: Peer review plus NIST co-authorship raises the credibility weight versus vendor-issued press results, and the consortium shape signals how US quantum-networking commercialization is being routed through federal labs.
